introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Citizenship Education 2 (0562), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- You are required to answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B and C.
- All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to different parts of questions are indicated.
- Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Question 1 (compulsory)**

Study this extract on National Integration and then answer questions (a) to (e) which follow. The maximum mark allocation for each sub-question is indicated in brackets.

> Cameroon has severally been hailed for holding on to its unity despite its geographical and cultural diversity, hence "Africa in miniature." According to the President of the Republic, this specificity of Cameroon is thanks to its continuous efforts at making the citizens feel at home wherever they find themselves in the country, a true legacy of our coming together in 1961.
>
> The Preamble of the Constitution states that, the people of Cameroon, proud of our linguistic and cultural diversity, an enriching feature of our national identity... solemnly declare that we constitute one and the same Nation, bound by the same destiny and assert our firm determination to build the Cameroon Fatherland on the bases of the ideals of fraternity, justice, and progress. It equally proclaims that humans without distinction of race, religion, sex or belief have inalienable and sacred rights. In this context the State ensures the protection of minorities, women and encourages and protects the family.
>
> In spite, of recent challenges towards the full realization of National Integration, the Government has remained unrelenting in its efforts.

*Source: Cameroon National Integration Strategy. MINJEC, 2015.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Identify by **name**, the President of the Republic mentioned in the passage.

(ii) Name **TWO** events that contributed to the process of "our coming together in 1961" (**line 4**).

(iii) In which way was the coming together mentioned above, further strengthened in 1972?

[(1 + 2 + 1) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The President of the Republic (1 mark)**

The President of the Republic mentioned in the passage is **Paul Biya**, Head of State of Cameroon since 1982.

**(ii) Two events that led to "our coming together in 1961" (2 marks)**

Any two of the following:

1. **The United Nations plebiscite of 11 February 1961**: the people of the Southern Cameroons voted to join the Republic of Cameroon (the Northern Cameroons chose to join Nigeria).
2. **The Foumban Constitutional Conference (July 1961)**: representatives of the Southern Cameroons and of the Republic of Cameroon met in Foumban to discuss the constitution of the new union.
3. **The reunification on 1 October 1961**, when the Federal Republic of Cameroon was born, made up of two federated states (East Cameroon and West Cameroon), with a federal constitution.

**(iii) How the union was strengthened in 1972 (1 mark)**

On **20 May 1972** a **referendum** was held and the people approved the end of the federal system. The **federation was replaced by a unitary state**, the **United Republic of Cameroon**, with one government, one parliament and one administration for the whole country. This brought the two parts of the country closer and strengthened national unity.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) In which year was the constitution mentioned in **line 5** adopted?

(ii) State **TWO** important innovations brought about by the constitution identified in (b) (i).

(iii) Identify any **ONE** major provision of the constitution mentioned in **line 6** that was effectively implemented after 2011.

[(1 + 2 + 1) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The year of adoption (1 mark)**

The Constitution of Cameroon now in force was adopted in **1996** (law of January 1996). It amended the 1972 constitution and was later revised in 2008.

**(ii) Two important innovations (2 marks)**

Any two of the following:

1. **The creation of a Senate**, which made Parliament bicameral (National Assembly and Senate).
2. **Decentralisation**: the Regions became decentralised local authorities, with regional councils, next to the councils.
3. **The creation of a Constitutional Council** to judge the constitutionality of laws and to settle electoral disputes.
4. **Constitutional recognition of the protection of minorities and of the rights of indigenous populations** in the Preamble.
5. A **limit on the number of terms** of the President of the Republic in the original text (this limit was removed by the 2008 revision).

**(iii) One major provision implemented after 2011 (1 mark)**

Any one of the following:

- **The setting up of the Senate**: the first senators took office in **2013**, many years after the Constitution had provided for this chamber.
- **The installation of the Constitutional Council**, whose members took office in **2018**.
- **The implementation of decentralisation through the Regions**, whose first regional councillors were elected in 2020.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) What do you understand by "inalienable and sacred rights" (**line 12**)?

(ii) Name **TWO** examples of inalienable rights.

(iii) State **ONE** institution put in place by the government of Cameroon, to protect Human Rights.

[(1 + 2 + 1) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Meaning (1 mark)**

"**Inalienable**" rights are rights that **cannot be taken away, sold, transferred or given up**, because every person has them from birth simply as a human being. "**Sacred**" means that these rights are **holy and must be respected by everyone**: nobody, including the State, may violate them.

**(ii) Two examples (2 marks)**

Any two of: the **right to life**, the **right to liberty and security**, the **right to equality before the law**, the **right to freedom of conscience and religion**, the **right to a fair trial**, the **right to dignity** (freedom from torture and slavery).

**(iii) One institution (1 mark)**

The **National Commission on Human Rights and Freedoms** (an independent body that receives complaints, investigates violations and promotes human rights). Other acceptable answers: the courts and tribunals, the Constitutional Council, the human rights departments of the Ministry of Justice.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Give **TWO** examples of minority groups that benefit from government protection in Cameroon.

(ii) Identify any **TWO** problems faced by minorities in Cameroon.

(iii) State any **ONE** measure taken by the Cameroon government to guarantee family protection.

[(2 + 2 + 1) marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two minority groups (2 marks)**

Any two of: the **indigenous forest peoples (the Baka and other Pygmy groups)**, the **Mbororo** (pastoralist) communities, **persons with disabilities** and other vulnerable groups (for example refugees and displaced persons).

**(ii) Two problems faced by minorities (2 marks)**

Any two of:

1. **Marginalisation and discrimination** in social life and in public affairs.
2. **Limited access to education and health services**, often because they live in remote areas.
3. **Land and resource problems**: loss of the forest or grazing land on which they depend.
4. **Lack of civil status documents** (birth certificates and identity cards), which prevents them from enjoying their rights.
5. **Weak representation** in local and national decision-making, and poverty.

**(iii) One measure to protect the family (1 mark)**

Any one of: the Constitution **states that the State protects the family**; laws on **marriage and the rights of children** (civil status and family law) and the **penal code** that punishes domestic violence; **family allowances** and social protection through social insurance; ministries in charge of **social affairs and of the family and women's empowerment** that run programmes for families.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e) Describe the manifestations of national integration in Cameroon.

[(3 marks)]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**National integration** is the process by which the many ethnic, linguistic and cultural groups of Cameroon come to feel and act as **one nation**. It shows itself in the following ways (any three, 1 mark each, with a short description):

1. **Official bilingualism**: English and French are both official languages, and the State promotes their use in administration, schools and public life (including through a national commission for bilingualism and multiculturalism).
2. **Regional balance** in the recruitment into the public service, in competitive examinations and in the government, so that every region is represented.
3. **National symbols and national events**: one flag, one anthem, one motto, and national celebrations such as the National Day (20 May) and Youth Day, in which all Cameroonians take part.
4. **Mixed schools and universities**, including bilingual schools, where pupils and students from all regions study together; school and university exchange programmes and the national civic and youth programmes.
5. **Inter-ethnic marriages, settlement and trade**: Cameroonians live, work, marry and do business in regions other than their own.
6. **National sport and culture**: national football and other teams bring all Cameroonians together; cultural festivals, music and art present the cultures of the different regions.
7. **Decentralisation and national institutions** (Parliament, the Armed Forces, the political parties) that bring together citizens from all over the country.
